hero.headline: US strikes Iranian radar sites as Kuwait reports missile and drone attacks
hero.body:
The United States struck Iranian radar sites around the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, while Kuwait reported coming under missile and drone attacks. American aircraft fired on multiple Iranian military locations, including sites on Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The US military confirmed the operations targeted radar installations.

Kuwait condemned what it described as repeated Iranian attacks on its territory. The country reported intercepting missiles and drones aimed at its air defenses. Americans were injured in an Iranian missile strike on a Kuwaiti air base, according to reports. The attacks represent a direct expansion of hostilities to a neighboring Gulf state that hosts US military personnel.

The escalation follows a fragile ceasefire that had been in place between the US and Iran. President Trump said the situation would "all work out well" despite the renewed military strikes by both nations. Iran also confirmed it carried out fresh strikes in the region, though specific details of Iranian operations were not provided.

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical waterway for global oil shipments, with roughly a fifth of the world's petroleum passing through the narrow passage. Any military conflict in the area threatens to disrupt energy markets and raise fuel prices worldwide. The strait sits between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula, with Qeeshm Island positioned at its narrowest point.

The weekend strikes mark a significant breakdown in recent diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions between Washington and Tehran. The involvement of Kuwait, a US ally that has maintained relatively stable relations with Iran compared to other Gulf states, suggests the conflict may be widening beyond direct US-Iranian confrontation. The injuries to Americans on Kuwaiti soil could further complicate efforts to restore calm in the region.

cards.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Orders Strikes on Hezbollah Stronghold in Beirut
cards.teaser: Benjamin Netanyahu directed the military to target Dahieh in response to attacks on Israeli civilians.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered strikes on Dahieh, a Hezbollah stronghold located in the suburbs of Beirut. Netanyahu stated the strikes are a response to attacks by Hezbollah against Israeli civilians.

The escalating conflict between Israel and the Lebanese militia marks a significant intensification of hostilities between the two sides. Dahieh has historically served as a base for Hezbollah operations and has been targeted in previous confrontations.

cards.headline: Trump Iran peace proposal divides Republicans
cards.teaser: President Trump's consideration of a deal with Iran that would ease sanctions has created a rift among Republican lawmakers.
cards.body:
President Trump is actively pursuing a peace agreement with Iran to end the conflict between the two countries, but the diplomatic effort has created significant divisions within the Republican Party that will dominate Senate discussions this week.

The proposed deal centers on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resolving several outstanding issues including Iran's nuclear program. According to reports, Trump has requested specific changes to Iran's latest proposal, particularly regarding control of the strait and the handling of Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile.

Pakistani mediators have been instrumental in keeping negotiations alive. Iran submitted a new proposal through Pakistan after direct talks between the two sides stalled. The proposal followed an all-night negotiation session in Islamabad in April, described as the highest-level engagement between Iran and the US since the 1979 revolution. However, Trump indicated dissatisfaction with Iran's latest offer, telling reporters "they're asking for things I can't agree to."

A ceasefire has been in place for more than three weeks, though the US and Iran have sporadically exchanged military strikes during this period. Pakistani officials view the continuation of the ceasefire as a significant achievement and believe a deal remains within reach.

The main sticking points involve Iran's nuclear program and control of the Strait of Hormuz. Trump has insisted Iran must commit to not acquiring nuclear weapons, which requires addressing uranium enrichment and the country's uranium stockpile. Iran has proposed charging fees to vessels passing through the strait as part of a broader deal. However, Trump this week suggested the Iranian blockade of the strait was more effective than bombing, while Iran's supreme leader hailed a "new chapter" for the waterway, indicating neither side appears ready to back down.

The Trump administration warned that shipping companies paying tolls to Iran for passage through the strait could face punitive sanctions, complicating Iran's proposed fee structure.

Defense hawks within the Republican Party, led by Senate Armed Services Committee Chair Roger Wicker, oppose any agreement that would provide sanctions relief to Iran. This resistance reflects broader tensions within the GOP over how to approach Iran policy, with traditional national security conservatives pushing back against diplomatic efforts.

The global economic stakes are substantial. The war launched in February has killed thousands of people and driven up energy prices worldwide. Pakistani officials emphasize that the conflict threatens not only regional peace but also the global economy and the livelihoods of millions, including in Pakistan, where monthly energy import bills have nearly tripled because of the war.

Pakistani diplomacy has expanded beyond direct mediation. Pakistan's military chief visited Tehran in April while the prime minister cultivated regional support by visiting Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Turkey. Pakistan's foreign minister also coordinated with international partners including the United Kingdom to encourage the peace process.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Chair Powell warns political pressure threatens central bank credibility
cards.teaser: Jerome Powell used a public speech to caution that political interference with the Federal Reserve could undermine public trust in the institution.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell delivered a warning about threats to the central bank's credibility during a speech accepting an award. Powell cautioned that political pressure on the Federal Reserve poses risks to the institution's ability to maintain public trust and execute monetary policy effectively.

Without naming specific officials, Powell framed his remarks around the importance of central bank independence. The speech comes amid ongoing debates about the relationship between the Federal Reserve and elected officials, and the extent to which political leaders should influence monetary policy decisions.

cards.headline: Trump administration plans quick asylum rejections without interviews
cards.teaser: Internal documents show the administration developing a system to rapidly reject asylum claims without conducting interviews.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is developing a plan that would allow immigration officials to quickly reject asylum applications without conducting interviews with applicants, according to internal documents. The proposal would represent a significant change to current asylum procedures, which typically include interviews to assess claims.

The policy would affect individuals seeking protection in the United States on the basis of persecution or fear of return to their home countries. Details about which types of cases would be subject to expedited rejection or what criteria would be used for these determinations were included in the internal documents but not publicly disclosed.

cards.headline: Schumer moves to eliminate Trump anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer announced an effort to kill what he called a $1.776 billion slush fund.
cards.body:
Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer announced that Democrats will work to eliminate the Trump administration's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. The fund stems from a settlement in Trump v. the Internal Revenue Service and would provide payouts to those claiming government weaponization against them. Schumer characterized it as a slush fund and plans to force Republicans to vote on eliminating it.

The fund has drawn widespread criticism, with critics arguing it resembles a scheme to reward political allies. More than a dozen Republican senators have reportedly urged the administration to reconsider the fund. According to polling, majorities of both Democrats and Republicans oppose it.

hero.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Orders Strikes on Hezbollah Stronghold in Beirut
hero.teaser: Benjamin Netanyahu directed the military to target Dahieh in response to attacks on Israeli civilians.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered strikes on Dahieh, a Hezbollah stronghold located in the suburbs of Beirut. Netanyahu stated the strikes are a response to attacks by Hezbollah against Israeli civilians.

cards.headline: France Seizes Sanctioned Russian Oil Tanker With British Support
cards.teaser: A British helicopter provided assistance during the operation conducted on Sunday, according to the UK defense ministry.
cards.body:
French authorities seized the Tagor, a Russian oil tanker subject to international sanctions, during an operation in the Atlantic on Sunday morning. The vessel was detained in international waters more than 400 nautical miles west of Brittany with assistance from British and other international partners.

President Emmanuel Macron announced the seizure, highlighting it as part of efforts to combat Russia's "shadow fleet"—vessels circumventing sanctions imposed following the invasion of Ukraine. A British helicopter provided aerial support during the operation, according to the UK Ministry of Defence.

cards.headline: Nicaraguan Indigenous Leader Brooklyn Rivera Dies in Government Custody
cards.teaser: The 73-year-old Miskito political leader had been held by the government since his arrest in 2023.
cards.body:
Brooklyn Rivera, a 73-year-old prominent Miskito Indigenous leader, has died following three years in prison under Nicaragua's governing regime. Rivera was arrested in 2023 and held in government custody until his death.

Rights groups have condemned both his lengthy detention and the circumstances of his death. Rivera was a major advocate for Indigenous rights and autonomy for the Miskito people, who inhabit the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua and Honduras.

cards.headline: Austria Opens Trial of Syrian Officers Accused of Torture
cards.teaser: The proceedings mark Austria's first prosecution of officials from the Assad regime.
cards.body:
Austria began a trial of two former Syrian government officials accused of torture during the Assad era. The case represents the first time Austria has prosecuted members of the previous Syrian regime. Syrian witnesses will have the opportunity to confront the two men directly during the proceedings.

The defendants are former officers from the Baath regime who are accused of carrying out torture. They had been living in Austria before facing charges. The trial gives victims a rare forum to present testimony about abuses they say they suffered under the Assad government.

cards.headline: More Documents About UK Ambassador Mandelson and Epstein to Be Released
cards.teaser: A second batch of files could create additional problems for British Prime Minister Keir Starmer.
cards.body:
A second batch of documents related to Peter Mandelson is set to be released. The files are expected to include private texts and WhatsApps that offer insight into how government functions, including information flows and internal disagreements.

The document release presents a challenge for Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who appointed Mandelson to his ambassadorial position. Mandelson was dismissed from the role due to his connections to Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted sex offender who died in 2019 while awaiting trial on federal sex trafficking charges.

cards.headline: Five Ebola Patients Recover and Leave Hospital in DR Congo
cards.teaser: Health officials emphasized that people with symptoms should seek medical help.
cards.body:
Five patients infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo have recovered and been discharged from the hospital. Health authorities are highlighting these cases to encourage others experiencing symptoms to seek medical attention promptly.

Officials emphasize that infected individuals can recover with proper medical care. The outbreak remains concentrated in Congo's eastern Ituri province, where confirmed cases have reached 282. Early treatment significantly improves survival rates for Ebola, a severe illness characterized by fever, bleeding, and organ failure.

cards.headline: Confirmed Ebola cases in Congo reach 282 as outbreak continues
cards.teaser: Congo reports 282 confirmed Ebola cases in eastern Ituri province with over 1,000 suspected infections total.
cards.body:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed 282 cases, with over 1,000 suspected cases reported overall. The outbreak is concentrated in the eastern Ituri province. The virus involved is the Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved treatment or vaccine currently exists.

Five patients have recovered from the infection and been discharged from the hospital. Health officials are urging people who develop symptoms to seek medical help immediately, noting that infected individuals can recover from the disease.

cards.headline: Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund faces scrutiny
cards.teaser: Congress and courts are examining a $1.8 billion fund created by the Trump administration.
cards.body:
Revised Card Text

A $1.8 billion fund created through a settlement in Trump v the Internal Revenue Service is facing scrutiny in Congress and the courts. The out-of-court agreement gives the Trump administration discretion over how the money is distributed, drawing criticism that the arrangement amounts to cronyism and corruption.

Opposition spans both parties, with more than a dozen Republican senators urging the administration to reconsider the fund. Polling shows majorities of both Democrats and Republicans oppose it, citing concerns that it could be used to reward political allies while indirectly benefiting the Trump family.

cards.headline: New York Mayor Mamdani skips Israel Day parade
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not attend the annual parade celebrating Israel on Fifth Avenue.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani declined to participate in the annual Israel Day Parade held on Fifth Avenue. The event drew over 50,000 marchers and spectators, with other state and city leaders attending. The parade celebrates Israel and typically attracts wide participation from elected officials.

Mamdani's absence marked a departure from typical mayoral participation in the event. New York leaders joined the march despite the mayor's decision not to attend. The parade took place against what organizers described as a changed backdrop, though specific details about what has changed were not elaborated in available reports.

cards.headline: UK wins court case over collapsed Rwanda asylum deal
cards.teaser: A court ruled the UK does not need to pay Rwanda after the asylum agreement fell through.
cards.body:
A court has ruled that the UK does not need to pay Rwanda following the collapse of an asylum deal between the two countries. Rwanda had sued the UK government for over £100 million, claiming it was owed after the agreement was breached.

The scheme, which was set up by Boris Johnson's administration to process asylum seekers in Rwanda, was scrapped by the Labour government on its first day in office. The court's decision means the UK will not be required to make any payments to Rwanda over the failed migrant deportation scheme.

cards.headline: France seizes Russian oil tanker with UK assistance
cards.teaser: French authorities seized a sanctioned Russian oil tanker with support from a British helicopter.
cards.body:
France seized the Russian oil tanker Tagor in the Atlantic on Sunday with support from British forces, including a helicopter. The vessel was detained in international waters more than 400 nautical miles west of Brittany. President Emmanuel Macron announced the operation, which targeted a ship subject to international sanctions on Russian oil exports.

The seizure is part of efforts to counter Russia's "shadow fleet"—vessels used to circumvent international sanctions. The operation involved cooperation between French and British forces, with the UK Ministry of Defence confirming the helicopter support provided during the detention.

hero.headline: Berkshire Hathaway to acquire homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion
hero.body:
Berkshire Hathaway announced plans to acquire Taylor Morrison Home Corporation for $6.8 billion in what marks the first major acquisition under Greg Abel, the designated successor to Warren Buffett. The deal represents a significant expansion of Berkshire's presence in the housing sector and signals confidence in the residential construction market.

The acquisition brings Taylor Morrison, one of the largest homebuilders in the United States, into Berkshire Hathaway's portfolio of companies. Taylor Morrison operates across multiple states and builds homes in various price segments, from entry-level to luxury properties. The purchase price reflects a premium on the homebuilder's current market valuation.

Greg Abel, who has been positioned to eventually take over leadership of Berkshire Hathaway from Warren Buffett, led the dealmaking efforts for this acquisition. The transaction represents Abel's first significant deal in his role and demonstrates his approach to capital deployment. Buffett publicly endorsed Abel's handling of the acquisition negotiations.

The deal comes as the housing market faces mixed signals, with high interest rates affecting affordability while housing supply remains constrained in many markets. Berkshire Hathaway already owns Clayton Homes, a manufactured housing company, giving the conglomerate experience in the residential housing sector. The addition of Taylor Morrison expands that footprint into traditional site-built homes.

The transaction requires regulatory approval and is expected to close in the coming months. Berkshire Hathaway, known for its long-term investment approach and willingness to deploy large amounts of cash for acquisitions, has been sitting on substantial cash reserves. The Taylor Morrison purchase represents a major use of that capital and reflects the company's assessment that residential construction offers attractive returns despite current market conditions.

cards.headline: Oil prices rise following military strikes between U.S. and Iran
cards.teaser: Crude oil prices climbed as investors assessed renewed military exchanges between the United States and Iran despite ongoing diplomatic negotiations.
cards.body:
Oil prices rose as the United States and Iran exchanged military strikes over the weekend. American aircraft bombed Iranian radar and drone control sites after Iran shot down a U.S. MQ-1 Predator drone. The strikes included targets on Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait also reported that its air defenses opened fire on Monday following drone and missile fire.

Investors are monitoring the situation closely, as the region supplies critical global energy production. The price gains reflect concerns about potential supply disruptions, even as both countries continue diplomatic negotiations.

cards.headline: Nvidia unveils new AI chip designed for personal computers
cards.teaser: The technology company introduced a chip aimed at bringing artificial intelligence capabilities to consumer PCs, with CEO Jensen Huang calling it a reinvention of computing.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced a new artificial intelligence chip specifically designed for personal computers. The release represents an expansion of AI processing power from data centers and specialized systems into consumer devices. CEO Jensen Huang described the move as the reinvention of the computer.

The chip launch positions Nvidia to capture a larger share of the personal computer market as manufacturers seek to integrate AI features into consumer devices. The announcement comes amid broader industry efforts to embed AI capabilities directly into hardware rather than relying solely on cloud-based processing.

cards.headline: Chinese military sought restricted Nvidia chips over six years, procurement records show
cards.teaser: An analysis of procurement documents reveals that China's People's Liberation Army openly attempted to acquire U.S. technology subject to export restrictions.
cards.body:
An analysis of six years of procurement records reveals that the People's Liberation Army made open attempts to acquire Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export restrictions. The records document sustained efforts by China's military to obtain the American semiconductor technology.

The findings raise concerns about how effectively U.S. export controls prevent advanced semiconductor technology from reaching Chinese military applications. The procurement data shows the PLA's persistent pursuit of chips that American officials have worked to keep out of military hands.

cards.headline: Stock markets rise on AI enthusiasm and Nvidia chip announcement
cards.teaser: U.S. stock futures climbed following Nvidia's new product release, with investor focus on artificial intelligence offsetting concerns about Middle East tensions.
cards.body:
Stock market futures climbed after Nvidia unveiled a new "superchip" designed to bring artificial intelligence capabilities directly to laptops and personal computers. The chip, called RTX Spark for Microsoft Windows, is designed to enable AI agents to replace traditional input methods like the mouse and keyboard. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described the development as the "reinvention of the computer."

The announcement intensified competition among major chipmakers, pitting Nvidia against Intel, Apple, Qualcomm and AMD in the race for PC-based AI dominance. Market gains persisted despite rising oil prices linked to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, suggesting investor appetite for AI-related stocks continued to outweigh concerns about energy costs and regional instability.

cards.headline: Pre-ChatGPT startups face pressure from rapid AI advancement
cards.teaser: Companies built before the emergence of large language models are struggling to compete as artificial intelligence reshapes technology markets.
cards.body:
A generation of technology startups founded before ChatGPT launched faces mounting competitive pressure from newer AI-powered alternatives. Companies that built products and services using earlier technology approaches are finding their market positions threatened by rapid advances in artificial intelligence capabilities.

The shift has created challenges for firms that went public or raised significant funding based on business models that predate the current wave of generative AI tools. Some companies are racing to integrate new AI features, while others are finding their core offerings less relevant in a market transformed by large language models.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes off Massachusetts coast with force equal to 300 tons of TNT
hero.body:
A meteor exploded off the coast of Massachusetts, creating a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT and causing a loud boom heard across the region. The explosion occurred as the meteorite entered Earth's atmosphere above Cape Cod Bay. Residents reported sightings from Delaware to Montreal, and footage captured the meteor's descent.

NASA stated that fragments from the meteorite may have landed in Cape Cod Bay and could potentially be recovered. The agency is analyzing the trajectory and impact data to determine the precise location where pieces might be found. The blast was powerful enough to generate reports of the explosion across multiple states and into Canada.

Meteors entering Earth's atmosphere at high speeds often create visible fireballs and sonic booms as they disintegrate from friction and pressure. The energy released during atmospheric entry can produce explosions comparable to conventional explosives, measured in tons of TNT equivalent. This particular meteor's 300-ton blast places it among the more substantial recent atmospheric entries detected over populated areas.

The event drew widespread attention due to its visibility across such a large geographic area and the intensity of the sonic boom. Witnesses described seeing a bright flash in the sky followed by a thunderous noise. Video footage from news stations showed the meteor's luminous trail as it descended toward the ocean. The explosion occurred over water, preventing any damage to populated areas or infrastructure.

Meteor events of this magnitude, while not exceptionally rare, serve as reminders of the constant influx of space debris entering Earth's atmosphere. Most meteors burn up completely before reaching the surface, but larger fragments occasionally survive to become meteorites. If pieces are recovered from Cape Cod Bay, they could provide scientists with material for studying the composition and origin of the meteor. NASA continues to monitor for additional reports and is coordinating with local authorities regarding potential recovery efforts.

cards.headline: CERN detects particle behavior that challenges known physics
cards.teaser: Physicists at the Large Hadron Collider observed a particle acting in ways current theory cannot explain.
cards.body:
Scientists at CERN detected strange particle behavior at the Large Hadron Collider that represents the strongest indication yet of physics beyond the Standard Model. The observation involves particles behaving in ways that current theoretical predictions cannot account for, reaching high statistical significance.

The detection occurred at the world's largest particle accelerator, where physicists routinely smash particles together at extremely high energies to study fundamental forces and matter. The anomaly suggests the existence of physical phenomena not explained by the Standard Model, the framework that has described particle physics for decades. The finding could point toward new particles or forces that scientists have not yet identified.

cards.headline: OpenAI model solves math problem unsolved for 80 years
cards.teaser: An artificial intelligence model from OpenAI found a solution to a famous mathematical problem that had stumped researchers since the 1940s.
cards.body:
OpenAI announced that one of its models successfully solved a longstanding mathematical problem that had remained unsolved for eight decades. The company published details of the solution, though the explanation has been described as complex and difficult to parse.

The breakthrough represents a significant advancement in AI's ability to tackle abstract mathematical reasoning that has eluded human mathematicians. Mathematical problems that have persisted for decades often require novel approaches or insights that traditional methods have failed to uncover. The solution demonstrates the potential for AI systems to contribute to pure mathematics research.

cards.headline: Nvidia introduces chip designed to run AI agents on personal computers
cards.teaser: The company launched its first PC-focused processors built specifically for running artificial intelligence agents locally.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced new processors designed to bring AI agent capabilities directly to laptops and desktop computers. The company introduced what it calls a superchip for consumer PCs, along with the DGX Station for Windows that puts trillion-parameter AI computing power on enterprise desks. Microsoft also announced the Surface Laptop Ultra as part of the hardware push.

The announcement triggered stock rallies for Arm, IBM, and Hewlett Packard, extending gains in software and chip companies positioned to benefit from local AI processing. Nvidia characterized the launch as a reinvention of the chip category for the AI agent era. The processors aim to enable users to run sophisticated AI models on their own hardware rather than relying on cloud-based processing.

cards.headline: Dell launches $699 touchscreen laptop to compete with Apple
cards.teaser: The XPS 13 represents Dell's most affordable version of the laptop line, undercutting Apple's MacBook Neo pricing.
cards.body:
Dell is launching a new XPS 13 laptop starting at $699 with a touchscreen display, positioning itself as a competitor to Apple's MacBook Neo. The company is offering an introductory promotion of $599 for students through September during back-to-school season, after which the standard price takes effect.

The XPS 13 will be available beginning in July. Dell's pricing strategy undercuts Apple's offering significantly, as the MacBook Neo is reported to cost over $2,000. The touchscreen feature differentiates Dell's laptop from Apple's current MacBook lineup.

cards.headline: AMD releases Radeon RX 9070 GRE graphics card globally at $550
cards.teaser: The graphics card, previously sold only in China, is now available worldwide at $549 to $550.
cards.body:
AMD launched the Radeon RX 9070 GRE graphics card for global sale starting June 2, priced at $549 to $550. The card was previously exclusive to the Chinese market but is now available for purchase internationally. The GPU is positioned to fill the gap between the RX 9060 XT and RX 9070 in AMD's product lineup.

The company also announced the Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 Series processors during the same product release event. The RX 9070 GRE uses AMD's RDNA 4 architecture and targets gamers looking for performance between the company's mid-range and higher-end graphics offerings. The global expansion makes the card available to consumers in markets where it was not previously sold.

cards.headline: Asus announces OLED handheld gaming device at Computex
cards.teaser: The ROG Xbox Ally X20 Bundle marks a 20th anniversary edition with an OLED screen.

hero.headline: James Milner retires after 24-year Premier League career
hero.body:
James Milner has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 40, concluding a remarkable 24-season career in the Premier League. The former England international made the announcement after spending his final three years at Brighton.

Milner began his career at Leeds, his boyhood club, and went on to become one of the most durable players in English top-flight history. He holds the record for the most Premier League appearances, reaching the milestone with 658 total appearances after playing against Brentford in February while representing Brighton. The achievement came after nearly a quarter century competing at the highest level of English football.

During his time in the Premier League, Milner represented several top clubs and earned 61 caps for the England national team. He became known throughout his career for his versatility, professionalism, and ability to adapt to different tactical systems and managers. His consistency across multiple generations of players and changing approaches to English football helped him maintain his position as a valued squad member even in his later playing years.

Those who worked with Milner throughout his career have consistently highlighted his dedication and work ethic. Michael Bridges, who played alongside him at Leeds, described him as "the most dedicated and professional young player" he had met, noting that Milner took the transition from school football to the first team entirely in stride. Bridges also remarked on Milner's intelligence as a footballer, his ability to read the game, and his impressive positioning and tracking back.

Steve Harper, who knew Milner during his time at Newcastle, praised his professionalism even as a teenager and said he remained grounded despite his incredible success. Curtis Davies, his England Under-21 teammate and fellow Aston Villa player, highlighted Milner's competitive drive to excel at everything, noting his commitment to maintaining peak physical condition and his desire to be the best in every aspect of his professional life.

Davies also suggested that Milner's primary motivation in his later years was breaking the appearance record previously held by Gareth Barry, another former Villa teammate. The determination and competitive edge that drove Milner throughout his career ultimately saw him achieve this significant milestone.

Milner's retirement leaves a notable gap in English football. His record of Premier League appearances represents a benchmark that current players will find difficult to match, cementing his legacy as one of the most consistent and reliable performers in the competition's history. Speaking about his career, Milner said he could never have dreamed of the journey his football life has taken him on.

cards.headline: Liverpool sacks manager Arne Slot
cards.teaser: Arne Slot was dismissed as Liverpool head coach, ending his tenure at the club.
cards.body:
Liverpool dismissed Arne Slot from his position as head coach on Saturday, 13 months after he won the Premier League title in his debut season. The sacking came following a dramatic decline in the team's performance during his second year.

In response, Slot published an open letter thanking Liverpool supporters for a connection that "goes beyond football." He stated the club has the foundations to compete at the highest level for years to come and is leaving Liverpool "exactly where it belongs: among Europe's elite." In his letter, Slot also reflected on difficult moments during his tenure, including the death of player Diogo Jota last summer.

cards.headline: Rugby league coach John Kear dies at 71
cards.teaser: John Kear, former England and Wales rugby league coach and broadcaster, has died.
cards.body:
John Kear, a former coach of both the England and Wales rugby league national teams, has died at age 71. He passed away on Sunday while travelling back from the Challenge Cup final.

Kear was a respected figure in rugby league, known for his contributions as both a coach and broadcaster. Former BBC rugby league correspondent Dave Woods paid tribute to him, describing Kear as one of rugby league's great characters whose passion for the sport defined his career.

cards.headline: Leah Williamson ruled out of England World Cup qualifiers
cards.teaser: England captain Leah Williamson will miss upcoming Women's World Cup qualifying matches.
cards.body:
England captain Leah Williamson has been ruled out of the Women's World Cup qualifying matches against Spain and Ukraine. Her absence is a significant blow to the national team ahead of these crucial fixtures.

The Lionesses will need to find replacements for their captain as they continue their push toward World Cup qualification without one of their key players.

cards.headline: ICC to trial pink balls in Test matches to address bad light
cards.teaser: The International Cricket Council will test pink balls to reduce play lost to poor lighting conditions.
cards.body:
The International Cricket Council has introduced a trial using pink balls in Test matches to reduce play lost due to bad light conditions. Bad light stoppages have long been a challenge in Test cricket, forcing umpires to suspend matches when visibility becomes poor.

The pink ball is designed to be more visible in low-light conditions than the traditional red ball, potentially allowing play to continue longer during evening sessions and reducing interruptions.

cards.headline: Pirates place pitcher Carmen Mlodzinski on restricted list
cards.teaser: The Pittsburgh Pirates have put right-hander Carmen Mlodzinski on their restricted list.
cards.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates placed right-handed pitcher Carmen Mlodzinski on the restricted list. The move takes Mlodzinski off the active roster and raises questions about his future with the team.

Mlodzinski's placement on the restricted list follows what commentators have described as justified anger over an unspecified situation. The restricted list designation means he is temporarily unavailable to the Pirates and not on the 40-man roster.

cards.headline: Illinois House blocks Chicago Bears stadium legislation
cards.teaser: The Illinois House did not advance a stadium bill for the Bears after the Senate approved it.
cards.body:
The Illinois House of Representatives declined to move forward with legislation for a new Chicago Bears stadium despite the bill clearing the state Senate. The House action came as the legislative session deadline passed without a deal.

Illinois lawmakers passed a budget but failed to reach an agreement on the Bears stadium proposal. The legislative impasse leaves the team's plans for a new facility uncertain and raises questions about the Bears' future at Soldier Field.

hero.headline: HBO's Euphoria to End After Season 3
hero.body:
HBO's drama series Euphoria will conclude with its third season, creator Sam Levinson has confirmed. The writer stated that the decision to end the show felt like "an honest ending," characterizing the story as "a tragic one in the end — but it's also the truth."

The series, which debuted in 2019, became a cultural phenomenon for its unflinching look at teenage life, addiction, and mental health issues. Zendaya stars as Rue Bennett, a recovering drug addict navigating high school, relationships, and trauma. The show has been notable for its distinctive visual style and willingness to tackle difficult subject matter.

Zendaya has earned two Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for her role. The second season aired in early 2022 and generated both critical praise and controversy due to its depictions of drug use, sexuality, and violence. Production on the third season experienced significant delays caused by scheduling conflicts and the 2023 writers' and actors' strikes.

The announcement comes as HBO and parent company Warner Bros. Discovery continue to reassess their programming strategy amid broader industry shifts. The network has renewed some major series while canceling others as part of ongoing cost-cutting efforts. Several cast members have pursued other prominent projects during the extended gap between seasons.

According to reports, tension has surfaced between the cast and Levinson in recent years. Some cast members appeared reluctant during recent promotional activities, with sparse social media engagement and ambiguous comments about the filming experience.

Based on early reviews of the available episodes, the third season takes a notably darker direction. Set five years after season two, the story follows Rue as she becomes entangled with a drug dealer to settle debts, eventually working as a courier between Mexico and the United States. The season also explores other characters' storylines, including Cassie's involvement in content creation and her relationship with Nate.

Critics have noted that while individual performances remain strong, particularly from Zendaya, Sydney Sweeney, and Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje, the overall tone has shifted toward bleakness. Some have observed that the show's approach to sex work and related themes feels contradictory, simultaneously voyeuristic and judgmental.

Levinson has described the season as connected to themes of surrender and redemption, and as a tribute to cast member Angus Cloud, who played Fezco and died in 2023 at age 25. The season also marks the final on-screen appearance of Eric Dane, who plays Nate's father, Cal.

The third season is available on Sky Atlantic and HBO Max. No official premiere date has been announced for new episodes, though production is expected to continue this year.

cards.headline: Zee Entertainment Secures FIFA Soccer Rights for India Through 2034
cards.teaser: Zee Entertainment Enterprises acquired broadcast and streaming rights to 39 FIFA soccer events in India, covering competitions through 2034.
cards.body:
Zee Entertainment Enterprises secured Indian broadcast and streaming rights to 39 FIFA soccer events spanning 2026 to 2034, including the FIFA World Cup 2026, FIFA World Cup 2030, and FIFA Women's World Cup 2027. The company announced the agreement on the first day of June.

The deal represents the first partnership between Zee and FIFA. The package includes age-group tournaments and futsal competitions in addition to the major World Cup events. The acquisition gives Zee control of soccer's most-watched events across both linear television and digital streaming platforms in India for the next eight years.

cards.headline: BBC Comedy Director Jon Petrie Joins Hat Trick Productions
cards.teaser: Jon Petrie left his position as BBC director of comedy to become creative director at independent production company Hat Trick.
cards.body:
Jon Petrie has left his position as the BBC's director of comedy to join Hat Trick Productions as creative director. Hat Trick is an independent production company behind comedy shows including Derry Girls, Have I Got News for You, Mastermind, and Whose Line Is It Anyway?

Petrie's move marks a transition from the public broadcaster to the independent sector, where he will oversee creative direction at one of the UK's leading comedy producers.

cards.headline: IMAX Returns to Hyderabad at Mahesh Babu's AMB Cinemas
cards.teaser: IMAX Corporation struck a deal for three new laser locations in India through AMB Cinemas, with the first opening at the Hyderabad theater co-owned by actor Mahesh Babu.
cards.body:
IMAX Corporation and Asian Cinemas agreed to open three new IMAX with Laser locations in India through the AMB Cinemas brand. The first location will open at AMB Classic in Hyderabad, a luxury cinema co-owned by Telugu film star Mahesh Babu, ahead of the release of Varanasi.

Varanasi is the upcoming film directed by S.S. Rajamouli. The new IMAX theater marks the format's return to Hyderabad. The expansion agreement between IMAX and Asian Cinemas focuses on bringing premium large-format screens to Indian markets through the AMB Cinemas chain, which operates luxury movie theaters.

cards.headline: UK Home Office Bars Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur From Entering Country
cards.teaser: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood blocked Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and broadcaster Cenk Uygur from entering the UK, preventing their attendance at SXSW London.
cards.body:
UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood barred Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and his uncle, broadcaster Cenk Uygur, from entering the United Kingdom. The decision prevents them from attending SXSW London, where they were scheduled to appear.

The Home Office issued the entry ban for Piker and Uygur ahead of the South by Southwest festival's London edition. Both were set to participate in programming at the event before the government action blocked their travel. The UK Home Office and SXSW London both issued statements following the announcement of the entry restrictions.

cards.headline: Mick Jagger Says Rolling Stones Will Tour Again After 2026
cards.teaser: Rolling Stones frontman Mick Jagger confirmed the band will not tour in 2026 but plans to return to the road as soon as possible.
cards.body:
Mick Jagger said he looks forward to touring with the Rolling Stones again. The musician confirmed the band will not tour in 2026 but stated a tour will happen as soon as possible.

Jagger did not specify when the Rolling Stones would resume touring or provide details about potential dates or locations. The band last toured in recent years, with Jagger now indicating fans will need to wait beyond 2026 for the next series of performances. The statement offers the first timeline information about the veteran rock group's future concert plans.

hero.headline: Trump Iran peace proposal divides Republicans
hero.teaser: President Trump's consideration of a deal with Iran that would ease sanctions has created a rift among Republican lawmakers.
hero.body:
President Trump is actively pursuing a peace agreement with Iran to end the conflict between the two countries, but the diplomatic effort has created significant divisions within the Republican Party that will dominate Senate discussions this week.

The proposed deal centers on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resolving several outstanding issues including Iran's nuclear program. According to reports, Trump has requested specific changes to Iran's latest proposal, particularly regarding control of the strait and the handling of Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile.

Pakistani mediators have been instrumental in keeping negotiations alive. Iran submitted a new proposal through Pakistan after direct talks between the two sides stalled. The proposal followed an all-night negotiation session in Islamabad in April, described as the highest-level engagement between Iran and the US since the 1979 revolution. However, Trump indicated dissatisfaction with Iran's latest offer, telling reporters "they're asking for things I can't agree to."

A ceasefire has been in place for more than three weeks, though the US and Iran have sporadically exchanged military strikes during this period. Pakistani officials view the continuation of the ceasefire as a significant achievement and believe a deal remains within reach.

The main sticking points involve Iran's nuclear program and control of the Strait of Hormuz. Trump has insisted Iran must commit to not acquiring nuclear weapons, which requires addressing uranium enrichment and the country's uranium stockpile. Iran has proposed charging fees to vessels passing through the strait as part of a broader deal. However, Trump this week suggested the Iranian blockade of the strait was more effective than bombing, while Iran's supreme leader hailed a "new chapter" for the waterway, indicating neither side appears ready to back down.

The Trump administration warned that shipping companies paying tolls to Iran for passage through the strait could face punitive sanctions, complicating Iran's proposed fee structure.

Defense hawks within the Republican Party, led by Senate Armed Services Committee Chair Roger Wicker, oppose any agreement that would provide sanctions relief to Iran. This resistance reflects broader tensions within the GOP over how to approach Iran policy, with traditional national security conservatives pushing back against diplomatic efforts.

The global economic stakes are substantial. The war launched in February has killed thousands of people and driven up energy prices worldwide. Pakistani officials emphasize that the conflict threatens not only regional peace but also the global economy and the livelihoods of millions, including in Pakistan, where monthly energy import bills have nearly tripled because of the war.

Pakistani diplomacy has expanded beyond direct mediation. Pakistan's military chief visited Tehran in April while the prime minister cultivated regional support by visiting Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Turkey. Pakistan's foreign minister also coordinated with international partners including the United Kingdom to encourage the peace process.

cards.headline: US strikes Iranian radar and drone sites
cards.teaser: The United States military struck radar and drone command sites in Iran over the weekend, US Central Command announced late Sunday.
cards.body:
The United States military struck Iranian radar and drone sites over the weekend, US Central Command announced Sunday. The attacks targeted facilities including those on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Central Command described the operations as self-defense strikes against Iranian radar and drone command and control sites.

The strikes occurred amid escalating tensions in the Persian Gulf region. Kuwait reported Iranian missile and drone attacks, condemning what it called "repeated" Iranian operations in the area. The military action underscores ongoing US-Iran hostilities even as the Trump administration explores diplomatic options with Tehran.

cards.headline: Schumer moves to eliminate Trump anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer announced an effort to kill what he called a $1.776 billion slush fund.
cards.body:
Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer announced that Democrats will work to eliminate the Trump administration's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. The fund stems from a settlement in Trump v. the Internal Revenue Service and would provide payouts to those claiming government weaponization against them. Schumer characterized it as a slush fund and plans to force Republicans to vote on eliminating it.

The fund has drawn widespread criticism, with critics arguing it resembles a scheme to reward political allies. More than a dozen Republican senators have reportedly urged the administration to reconsider the fund. According to polling, majorities of both Democrats and Republicans oppose it.

cards.headline: Senate returns amid immigration bill stalemate
cards.teaser: Negotiations on an immigration enforcement funding package collapsed after the White House announced a separate controversial fund.
cards.body:
The Senate will return to session after missing a deadline to deliver an immigration enforcement funding package to President Trump. Negotiations on the measure broke down more than a week ago following the White House's announcement of a separate anti-weaponization fund.

The immigration bill was expected to reach the president's desk by the original deadline, but the creation of the controversial fund derailed the process. The Senate is now preparing for a showdown over both the immigration measure and the anti-weaponization fund as lawmakers return to Capitol Hill.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra emerges as California governor frontrunner
cards.teaser: The former Health and Human Services secretary has gained significant momentum ahead of the state's primary election.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra is positioned to finish as one of the top contenders in California's race to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom. His strong showing marks a significant turnaround after polling in single digits just months earlier.

Several factors have boosted Becerra's momentum, including former Representative Eric Swalwell's departure from the race. California's unusual primary system, combined with recent scandals and a relatively low-profile candidate field, have made the governor's race particularly unpredictable this cycle.

cards.headline: Chemical plant incidents fuel safety rule debate
cards.teaser: Recent industrial accidents have intensified criticism of Trump administration efforts to roll back chemical safety regulations.
cards.body:
Critics are outraged over the Trump administration's push to roll back chemical safety rules amid a series of dangerous industrial incidents. Last week, approximately 50,000 residents in Southern California were evacuated due to an overheating chemical tank that posed an explosion risk. Evacuation orders were later lifted.

The timing of these chemical plant disasters has intensified debate over deregulation efforts. Opponents argue that weakening safety regulations puts communities at greater risk during a period marked by active industrial accidents.

cards.headline: Trump backs federal authority over prediction markets
cards.teaser: The president is supporting efforts to block state restrictions on prediction market platforms.
cards.body:
President Trump is supporting an effort to block state restrictions on prediction markets as federal and state regulators compete for authority over the platforms. The legal dispute has created divisions within the Republican Party over regulatory jurisdiction.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has brought cases against more than half a dozen states over their efforts to regulate prediction markets. The administration's position favors federal oversight through the CFTC rather than allowing individual states to impose their own restrictions on these platforms.
